- Summary: Fixed subtitle ASR popup jumping to top-left corner in the video player: showAsrContextMenu was anchored to opt-generate-subtitle which had just been display:none'd by the click handler, so getBoundingClientRect returned all zeros. Rerouted the anchor to the persistent btn-subtitles CC button and changed the positioner to right-align (mirrors the subtitles-menu right:0 layout) and prefer opening upward when the anchor is in the lower 40 percent of the viewport. Also fixed the player right-click Enhance Video action which was calling upscaleVideo(itemPath) as a bare string, discarding the appSettings vsrQuality/vsrScale/vsrChroma the user had configured; now sends {path, quality, scale, chroma} same as card-events.js. Modernized ImageMagick denoise op from deprecated '-median 3' to '-statistic Median 3' (silences the deprecation warning that was printed to console on every image denoise). Diagnosed the audio-normalization pipeline (Demucs vocal isolation, ASR subtitles, translation synthesis): torchaudio 2.10 now delegates all save/load through torchcodec, which requires FFmpeg 4-7 shared .dll files on the load path. venv had no torchcodec â€” installed torchcodec 0.14 via pip. System has FFmpeg 6.1.1 static (Gyan.FFmpeg) on PATH and FFmpeg 8.1 shared (Gyan.FFmpeg.Shared) also present, but torchcodec supports only 4-7 and needs the shared build. All three AI voice paths remain broken until an FFmpeg-7 shared build is installed and its bin/ added to PATH before Python starts. Confirmed working: RealESRGAN image super-resolution (RTX 3060 detected, output produced), ImageMagick denoise/edge, nvvfx module for RTX VSR (imports cleanly). Timestamp: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:24

- Summary: Fixed WebM/thumbnail preview generation silently failing since commit e838f61 (2026-06-17). Root cause: the atomic-tmp scheme renamed ffmpeg outputs to .jpg.tmp/.webm.tmp but ffmpeg cannot infer muxer format from a .tmp suffix. A prior uncommitted patch added -f webm before webmWritePath in 4 places, but the 3 thumbnail ffmpeg calls still had no -f flag, so every thumb generation failed. The atomic-commit gate (thumbTmpOk && webmTmpOk) then discarded any successfully-produced webm because the thumb was missing, raising 'FFmpeg produced incomplete output'. Additionally js/progress.js showed 'Preview generated!' on failure because it only checked percent===100 and ignored data.error/label='Preview failed'. Fix: added -f image2 before thumbWritePath in all 3 ffmpeg thumbnail commands in src/previews.js; taught js/progress.js to show 'Preview failed: <file>' when data.error is set; extended tests/manual_webm_update_regression_test.js to assert >=3 image2-forced thumb outputs. Verified with real ffmpeg 8.1 that .jpg.tmp+image2 emits valid JPEG and .webm.tmp+webm emits valid WebM. Both regression tests pass. Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:05
- Commands:
  - `node tests/manual_webm_update_regression_test.js`
  - `node tests/preview_path_regression_test.js`
  - `ffmpeg -y ... -f image2 test.jpg.tmp`
- Files:
  - `src/previews.js`
  - `js/progress.js`
  - `tests/manual_webm_update_regression_test.js`

- Summary: Fix cpu-upgrade OOM on SfM jobs (root cause of 6a3fc7875f9c8079e0fb703c exit 137 OOMKilled). (1) ns-process-data now invoked with --num-downscales 0 instead of 3 — skips the 1x/2x/4x/8x image pyramid that splatfacto never reads. The parallel pool that built it peaked RAM above 32 GB on 500 frames at 1920x1080. (2) os.environ.setdefault(OMP_NUM_THREADS, 4) at top of main() so every COLMAP subprocess (feature_extractor, sequential_matcher, vocab_tree_matcher in standard + refine paths) inherits the cap. 8 vCPU * full SIFT parallelism was multiplying peak memory by 8x. Combined: keeps peak RSS under 32 GB for refine-scale joint sets too. Reviewed other 4 recent ERROR jobs and confirmed they were unrelated (CUDA driver on CPU node from pre-revert state, old worker image without --sfm-only, 20-frame test too few for mapper init). Pushed worker; Space RUNNING_BUILDING. Plan once built: queue cloudy refine against sunny base local-run-20260614-234541 via headless_remote_run.py --preset refine --refine-from local-run-20260614-234541 --video cloudy1 --video cloudy2 --yes.

Hosting analysis: greencloud has 6.0GB available RAM, load avg 0.04, 24-day uptime - comfortably hosts the full RAG (~2GB peak when both BGE-small embedder + BGE-reranker-base loaded). - Summary: tech-oracle: cross-encoder reranker added to RAG pipeline (Tue, 23 Jun 2026). User flagged we forgot reranking. Also raised Qwen3 question - clarified Gemini does NOT use Qwen3 (uses Google's own text-embedding-005), but Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B IS a strong open option (~+8-9 MTEB points over BGE-small). Recommended adding reranker BEFORE swapping embedder because the specific failure we saw (Chrome-Stable-Update scoring 0.65 against macOS-Photos query by 'update' keyword) is a textbook cross-encoder fix; Qwen3 swap is corpus-density-bound. Build: tech_oracle/rag/rerank.py wraps fastembed.rerank.cross_encoder.TextCrossEncoder (ONNX, no torch dep). Default BAAI/bge-reranker-base (~1GB, ~280M params). Outputs sigmoid-normalized 0-1 scores. retrieve_related_per_item now does two-stage flow by default: bi-encoder recall (pull top_k*5 at min_score 0.45) then cross-encoder precision (drop <0.4 rerank, return top_k). SearchHit.score gets replaced with the rerank score so downstream prompts see the more meaningful number. CLI rag search is rerank-on by default with --no-rerank escape; output table shows both rerank and bi-encoder scores. Live test on the actual 65-item corpus PROVED the value: 'my printer wont print after windows update' query - bi-encoder had near-flat 0.67-0.73 top-5, reranker found ONE clearly-best HP-driver-complaint item and promoted 0.674->0.821 while demoting all other printer chatter to <0.15. 'macos icloud photos stuck' query - bi-encoder returned 8 false-positives in 0.55-0.57 band (Chrome updates, unrelated printer items); reranker zeroed EVERY ONE to 0.000 (corpus genuinely has no macOS-Photos content; correct behavior). Distribution is decisively bimodal vs bi-encoder mushy 0.4-0.7: rerank says match=0.5+, plausible=0.1-0.5, no-match=<0.05. Cost: one-time 90s 1GB download; ~30-50ms per pair on CPU; ~5-7s extra per synthesis batch (well within budget). UTF-8 stdout fix applied to cli.py module

- Summary: tech-oracle: embedding model benchmark + RAG-augmented synthesis wired (Tue, 23 Jun 2026). User asked for concrete numbers on bigger embedding models + live-vs-cron tradeoff, then to wire retrieval into synthesis. Benchmark inline (tests/benchmark_embed.py + resource_compat.py) compared BGE-small vs BGE-base on the same 65-item live corpus. Results: BGE-base is 2.8x slower per item (193.9 ms vs 69.5 ms), uses ~500MB more RSS (1567 vs 1068 MB), disk 1.75x (0.223 MB vs 0.127 MB at 65 items). Surprise: BGE-small actually scored HIGHER on direct-match queries (printer 0.731 vs 0.707, outlook 0.597 vs 0.541) - BGE-base's only clear win was better off-topic category discrimination (returned tech-news instead of printer noise on spacex query). Recommendation: stay on BGE-small until corpus reaches ~10k items. Live-vs-cron: both invisible on Clopeux at our load (sustained <0.1% CPU, ~120ms bursts per item). Cron simpler operationally; daemon offers freshness in minutes which we dont need. Build: tech_oracle/rag/retrieve.py with retrieve_related_per_item(items, rag_store, top_k, min_score) and hit_to_compact helper. Filters items in current batch out of results (only HISTORICAL context surfaces). Prompts: _compact_item now takes optional related[] argument; build_user_message takes related_past_items dict[item_id, list[dict]] and appends a NOTE telling the model to use them for dedup/clustering only - never for citations. Synthesize signature gained rag_store/rag_top_k/rag_min_score kwargs (defaults: 3 / 0.65); cleanly no-ops if lancedb/fastembed unavailable. CLI predict has --rag --rag-top-k --rag-min-score --lance flags. End-to-end test on the consumer fixture with --rag --refine: 2m50s wall, 12919 tokens, 7 predictions all with grandma-readable discrete step bullets, no-fix predictions correctly hit the 'Wait for the vendor' fallback + refine notes. Tracing what RAG

Picked the lightweight path the user worried about: ONNX-runtime BGE-small-en-v1.5 (no torch dep; ~150-300MB RAM, CPU-only) via fastembed, lancedb as embedded single-process vector store (no etcd/MinIO sidecars unlike Milvus). New SQLite migration: indexed_at column + items_indexed_idx. New store methods: recent_unindexed, mark_indexed, get_by_ids; stats() now reports unindexed count. New CLI: tech-oracle rag {index,search,stats}. UTF-8 stdout reconfigure at cli.py module top to fix UnicodeEncodeError from emoji in Reddit titles (Windows cp1252 codec breaks Rich tables on U+1F62B etc). Smoke test on the 65-item corpus: cold first-run 14.93s including 5-file ~6s model download; warm subsequent embedding ~120ms/item; lancedb disk 0.143 MB for 65 vectors (projected ~140MB at 100k); per-query warm latency ~200ms. Real semantic search proved working: 'my printer wont print after windows update' returned r/printers items with scores 0.731-0.712 (no literal word match - true semantic recall); 'outlook keeps crashing' returned 0.575 max (correctly low - we have ZERO outlook items in the index yet, signal scaling exactly as expected); 'spacex starship mars rocket' returned no hits above 0.5 (no false positives on unrelated queries). Resource verdict: invisible on a desktop being actively used - ComfyUI

- Summary: tech-oracle 8B enrichment worker (Mon, 22 Jun 2026 22:10). Added the per-item enrichment stage that turns sparse RSS items into rich records ready for 70B/8B synthesis. (a) Schemas: new EnrichmentOutput Pydantic model with summary/severity/tags/entities/raw_excerpt/is_low_information; exported from package root. (b) Module: tech_oracle/enrich/{__init__,prompts,worker}.py. enrich_one(item, client) returns merged_item + EnrichmentOutput + model_id + usage. Tags are union-merged with feed defaults, entities dict-merged with enriched values winning, raw_excerpt only overwrites if model provides one. Hard prompt rules: don't invent versions/numbers, leave entity keys absent rather than guess, write for non-technical 58-year-old grandma persona, severity is consumer-impact (not vendor importance), set is_low_information=true on thin Reddit-title-only items. JSON-mode, temperature 0.1, max_tokens 900. (c) Store: added enriched_at/enrichment_model/is_low_information columns with idempotent ALTER TABLE migration for existing DBs. New methods: recent_unenriched(), update_enriched(item, model, is_low_info). stats() now reports unenriched + low_information counts. (d) CLI: ech-oracle enrich [--limit N] [--source X] [--hours H] [--model M] [--dry-run] [--db PATH]. Pulls unenriched items, calls 8B per-item, merges back into store. Reports tokens used and ok/fail counts. (e) Live smoke test on real r/printers items: 8/9 successful enrichments at ~1500-1800 tokens each (~20-25s for 6 items). 1 transient NIM failure, skipped and picked up on next pass. The 'What do i do?' Reddit thread - originally tags=[reddit,printer,consumer] and entities={} - got enriched to entities={company:hp, product:designjet-t730}, severity=low, is_low_information=true, with the body mined for a useful narrative summary. The model correctly grounded entities from the post body that the title alone gave nothing on. (f) README updated with before/after table and pipeline diagram now showing ingest -> 8B enrich -> SQLite ->

- Summary: Built Prom-King/tech-oracle (Mon, 22 Jun 2026 16:00): a focused synthesis service for the tech-support prediction pipeline. Calls NVIDIA NIM Llama 3.3 70B Instruct (free build.nvidia.com endpoint via NGC_API_KEY/NVIDIA_API_KEY) to turn pre-ingested news/changelog items + deterministic Postgres breakage scores into ranked TechPrediction objects. Layout: uv-managed pyproject.toml (Python 3.11+), src/tech_oracle/{client,schemas,prompts,synthesize,cli,api}.py, tests/fixtures/sample_request.json (handcrafted realistic 2026-06 batch: KB5039340 Win11 24H2 wifi, Anthropic claude-2-5-sonnet deprecation, Copilot Pro price hike 2026-07-15, macOS 15.7 Keychain visibility change, Chrome 141 WebGPU/extensions breakage, NVIDIA 558.20 HDR/OBS bug + 6 breakage scores). Hard rules baked into the prompt: JSON-only output, every prediction must cite source_item_ids, must use provided scores as-given (no inventing stats), calibrated confidence (high needs >=2 corroborating items AND strong vendor breakage history), bias toward missing over inventing, kebab-case prediction_id slugs. Stack is dependency-light: httpx + pydantic + fastapi + typer + rich. Smoke test against real NIM 70B: 1m11s, 4975 tokens (3127 in / 1848 out), 6 predictions all schema-valid, all with citations and reasoning that references the supplied breakage scores. Calibration looked right: only the KB5039340 wifi item got HIGH/next_24h; the Anthropic deprecation 3 months out correctly got LOW/watch. Two fixes during testing: bumped default NIM timeout 120s->300s (env-overridable as NIM_TIMEOUT) because 70B with JSON mode + heavy prompt regularly takes >2min on free tier; relaxed PredictionResponse.usage from dict[str,int] to dict[str,Any] because NIM returns prompt_tokens_details=None. Service is library + CLI + FastAPI POST /predict, all hitting the same synthesize() function. Not deployed - lives locally under Prom-King/tech-oracle/ pending downstream pipeline pieces (Brave Search/RSS ingester, 8B enrichment worker, Postgres scoring DB, publishing CMS).

So qbit WebUI is accessible tailnet-wide at http://100.67.25.118:8081 (nginx vhost + UFW 8081/tailscale0 already existed). Jackett restored for Comet's scraper. Root cause: pornstars.gender is a Postgres ENUM (gender) but the filter does gender = ANY($N::text[]), which Postgres rejects without a cast. - Summary: Round 3 feedback fixes â€” eight items. (1) CRITICAL bug fix: prompts/textareas were uneditable because FlowCanvas initialized rfNodes from storeNodes once and never re-synced. Added a useEffect in FlowCanvas that propagates store data changes (params, label) to rfNodes while leaving position/measured state untouched (preserves the visibility:hidden fix from earlier sessions). Identity-checks on params and label avoid spurious re-renders. (2) Toast system: new src/ui/components/Toast.tsx with module-level event hub (pushToast/dismissToast from anywhere) and ToastHost mounted at App root; renders top-right stack with auto-dismiss (6s default, 4s for success); three tones (error/success/info) with matching tokens. App.tsx now pushes 'success' on clean run, 'error' on per-node or top-level failure + auto-opens the inspector. (3) Execution errors moved to TOP of NodeParamPanel â€” banner with the failure detail + a Reset button; the old bottom error block was removed. Per-node text/json outputs still render below (image results render inline ON the comfyui_workflow node). (4) Removed the auto-created Display node from loadFromComfyWorkflow; the master flow is now just the single comfyui_workflow node, with results rendering inline (gallery + thumbnails). Eliminates the disconnected 'Result' node that felt orphaned. (5) Inline image result on ComfyUIWorkflowNode: when the workflow succeeds and the result has imageUrl/imageUrls, the gallery renders inside the node card itself; click any thumb opens full-size in a new tab. (6) New InlineSeedInput in canvas/nodes/inline.tsx â€” number input with a dice button (Lucide Dice5) that fills a 31-bit random int. ComfyUIWorkflowNode routes any input key named 'seed' through this control. (7) Size presets dropdown â€” when a workflow exposes both 'width' and 'height' in input_paths, a single 'size' InlineSelect drives both (512Â², 768Â², 1024Â², portrait/landscape variants, Custom reveals manual w/h number inputs). Exported SIZE_PRESETS array from inline.tsx. (8) NodeId pill â€” small mono badge at the bottom of every node card showing 'node#<short-id>'; tooltip on hover reveals the full id. shortenNodeId helper formats numeric/short/UUID ids consistently. (9) Persisted last-used inputs: ComfyUIWorkflowNode reads localStorage['vw:lastInputs:<workflow_id>'] on mount if all inputs are empty, prefills non-image fields (upload tokens excluded â€” they expire); debounced 400ms save on every input change. Each user gets their own browser-local memory of last prompt/seed/size per workflow. Deployed dist (assets/index-BxACQy3N.js).

For large folders or cloud directories (like iCloud Photos with 2,100+ items), this ran over 6,000 synchronous I/O operations (fs.existsSync) in a single loop on the main process thread, blocking the Electron main thread and triggering a native access violation crash/watchdog lock. Optimized the handler in previews.js to skip automatic background previews for cloud-backed directories (iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox, etc.) and limited active batch size to 80 items in other folders. Rebuilt installer successfully.

- Summary: Landed A2: full real-time progress + cancel for comfyui_workflow nodes. Backend (vaultwares-pipelines): added websockets dependency (16.0) to .venv + requirements.txt. _execute_comfyui_graph now takes optional progress_cb + cancel_event args. Spawns _comfyui_ws_listener as an asyncio.Task that subscribes to ws://127.0.0.1:8188/ws?clientId=<id>, filters events by prompt_id, calls progress_cb with executing/progress/executed/execution_error/execution_success/execution_cached events. If cancel_event is set during execution, POSTs to ComfyUI's /interrupt and raises RuntimeError('canceled'). _execute_workflow_run plumbs both through. Job worker creates: (a) a progress_cb closure that maintains a progress_state dict and writes it to job.progress with throttling (~5 Hz), (b) a watch_cancel asyncio.Task that polls the job record once per second and sets cancel_event when status==canceled. JobSummary/JobDetail gained a progress field. New GET /jobs/recent endpoint (registered before /jobs/{job_id} to avoid the same path-conflict the validation endpoint hit) returns the caller's most recently-updated job, filterable by kind and CSV status; admins see all jobs, non-admins only their own (matched via requested_by.username or special 'vault-flows' tag). Frontend (vault-flows): listed JobSummary + JobProgress types in client.ts; getRecentJob(opts) handles the 'null' body case; cancelJob(id) calls POST /jobs/{id}/cancel. New ExecutionProgressOverlay.tsx renders a fixed bottom-right card while executionStatus==='running' â€” polls /jobs/recent at 1 Hz, shows a pulsing accent dot, progress bar (when total>0), current message, node + step counter, elapsed time, and a Cancel button that calls cancelJob. App.tsx mounts the overlay. Verified end-to-end: started a 30-step run, observed live step progress (poll showed step 4/12, then step 2/30 etc, with current node id 3), POST /jobs/{id}/cancel mid-execution â†’ worker tripped /interrupt â†’ /flows/run returned with error='ComfyUI workflow was canceled', final job status=canceled. Deployed dist (assets/index-DCi4ZtfE.js) atomically.

Frontend (src/api/client.ts): setToken/getToken now read/write sessionStorage key 'vw_jwt' with try/catch fallback to in-memory. Added clearToken() for use on stale-token detection. App.tsx: useEffect on mount that, if getToken() is set, calls getMe() and either rehydrates currentUser (success) or calls clearToken()+nulls user (401). This makes page refresh in the same tab keep the user logged in, while tab close still clears the token. Pipelines (.env): JWT_TTL_SECONDS=3600 â€” verified via login -> JWT payload exp-iat=3600s. - Summary: Three workflow-toolchain improvements addressing 'workflow runs in ComfyUI but fails validation' false positives. (1) Converter (convert_proven_workflows.py): skips nodes with mode==2 (muted) and mode==4 (bypassed); for bypassed nodes, rewires consumer links from bypassed_node.output[N] to whatever feeds bypassed_node.input[N], following chains of bypasses. This is exactly what ComfyUI's editor's 'Bypass' mode does at runtime. Eliminates dangling links + 'missing model' false positives where the referenced model was in a bypassed node. (2) Fixer (fix_workflows.py): smarter _core_key() that strips quant markers (FP16/FP8/Q2_K/etc), distillation markers (DMD/DMD2/distilled), AIO/base tags, and minor-version suffixes (V1.0/V1.1/v1-1) â€” so different-quant or patch-version files of the same base model are treated as drop-in substitutes. Closest_match() now uses the core-key tier as high-confidence matching (returns first match, prefers top-level files over nested copies). Also added Pass 3: normalize_load_image_widgets() replaces baked-in LoadImage filenames with a placeholder ('000.jpeg' from D:\\comfyui\\resources\\comfyui\\inputs) so ComfyUI's validator passes; the worker overrides at runtime. (3) Diagnostic (dump_workflows_diagnostic.py): validate_locally() now exempts LoadImage's image input from validation for any node referenced by step.image_inputs[] â€” runtime-overridden inputs are never structurally broken from the worker's POV. Re-seeded: 13/13 workflows now match the fixed JSONs (muted nodes dropped, bypasses rewired). New verdict tally: PASS=3 (biglove-photo, ipadapter-faceswap, z-image-turbo-text2img), BLOCKED_SUBGRAPH=4 (custom-realistic, flux-conditioner-sampler-upscaler, qwen-image-text2img, gonzalomo-dmd-v30), BLOCKED_UNKNOWN_PACK=3 (copilot/flux2-klein-faceswap/wan22 â€” AI-invented), BROKEN_WIRING=2 (basic-lora-text2img orphan upscale chain, qwen-edit-multi-angle unwired CLIP), BLOCKED_MISSING_MODEL=1 (openpose-i2i), VALIDATION_OTHER=1 (qwen-image-edit-4step references muted ReferenceLatent). All remaining issues are real workflow content problems requiring editor surgery.
